text: Lemma 15 [on paper] (where $w$ lives). Let $G$ have class $c=k+1$, $x_i^{E_i}=P_i\in\gamma_k$, $E_j\mid A_{ij}$, and $g_1\in(\gamma_k)^{E_1}\gamma_c$, $g_2\in(\gamma_k)^{E_2}\gamma_c$ (the pairing with multiplier 1). Then $$w=[x_2,x_1^{A_{12}}]=\prod_l[x_2,d_l]^{-a_lA_{12}/E_1}\qquad(P_1=\textstyle\prod_ld_l^{-a_l}).$$ Proof. For $y,z\in\gamma_k$, $[x_i,yz]=[x_i,y][x_i,z]$ and $[x_i,y^{E_i}]=[x_i^{E_i},y]=[P_i,y]=1$ ($[x_i,y]$ is central, $\gamma_k$ is abelian). So $u_{12}u_{13}=[x_1,g_1]=1$ and $u_{23}=[x_2,h_{23}]=[x_2,g_2][x_2,h_{21}]^{-1}=[x_2,x_1^{A_{12}}]$. $\square$

Steps (1) and (4) go one level further: $64X_1^2=8E_1X_1^2\in\Delta^5$ (Lemma 13 for $x_1$, $s=0$: $e_2=1$, $E_1\mid8$; $e_3=4$) gives the binomials of $x_1$ in $\Delta^7$, and $1024X_2^2X_5=(16E_2X_2^2)X_5$ with $1024X_2^2\in\Delta^6$ (Lemma 13, $s=1$) is in $\Delta^7$. Step (3) does not: $64X_2^2D_3=(E_2X_2)X_2D_3$ has the certified level $2+1+3=6$ and no more, and $64$ is the exponent that the relator of $x_1$ gives ($a_3N/E_1=4\cdot128/8$). So the carrier lifts its own part (the $d_2$-part) by two levels over the pairing (from $1+1+k$ to $\ge2k+1$), and the stop is in the part it does not carry.
